area: Existing plans and status ledger for M365 / Google / Copilot / Gemini integration work
summary:
The canonical ecosystem plan is BK28 (TASKS.md:395-551, docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md). It keeps LawHand as the system of record for matter identity, permissions, review and audit. Microsoft 365 and Google may supply context for the signed-in user, but agents may only read and propose; they never send, docket, file, clear conflicts or replace files (plan:34-57, 174-185).

**Recorded Copilot/Gemini direction**
- The first commercial wedge is a Microsoft "LawHand Matter Agent": Copilot Studio / Microsoft 365 Copilot connected to the existing OAuth 2.1 Workspace MCP (ECO-09 to ECO-13).
- ECO-19 is a later Google Workspace add-on (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs).
- ECO-21 is a Gemini Enterprise MCP/A2A pilot. It is gated until the Microsoft agent passes its matter-match, citation, review and margin tests.
- ECO-20 allows Gemini only as approved API-key / Cloud-Billing capacity behind LiteLLM.

**Explicitly ruled out**
- Using a personal Google One, Google AI or Microsoft Copilot subscription as LawHand inference capacity (plan:55-57, 99-106, 763).
- Marketing the agent as included with Microsoft 365. Copilot licensing must be checked for each tenant (plan:200-204).
- Broad mailbox ingestion, or a second "shadow" copy of the matter database inside Microsoft or Google (plan:771-772).
- One SharePoint site per routine matter.

**What has shipped**
- Security, reliability and observability fixes (remediation phases 0-2).
- Org-owned Google Shared Drive roots.
- Separate Personal Google and Google Workspace modes. This is the substance of ECO-17, but it is still unchecked in TASKS.md.
- Sending client mail from the user's own connected mailbox (Mail.Send / gmail.send).
- Calendar push of tasks.
- Teams channel notifications.
- Workspace MCP with read and propose tools, including propose_document_from_template, propose_client_email and propose_client_sms.

**Not started or incomplete**
- Every Copilot/Gemini agent item (ECO-09 to ECO-16 and ECO-18 to ECO-22).
- Microsoft app-only access with Sites.Selected.
- Delta sync and webhooks.
- The Office add-in: only Slice 0 exists, behind pilot flags, with four actions.
- The Word Template Builder add-in (W2): not started.

**Conflicts with the recorded direction**
- A tenant bring-your-own-key route named "gemini"/"copilot" bypasses LiteLLM, and "copilot" actually means an Azure OpenAI key.
- By default, Microsoft 365 tenants store matter files in the connecting admin's personal OneDrive, which the storage design itself rates at risk.
- A Teams app package is checked in, but the tab cannot load inside Teams.

**Constraint for implementation**
Per the S1.02 ownership record, only the BE owner may change api.js signatures and only FE-A may edit MatterDetailPage (core-ux-s1-02:37,30).

defects.title: Teams app tab cannot render inside Teams: edge forbids framing and there is no Teams SSO
defects.detail: The server-level `X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN` and CSP `frame-ancestors 'self'` are inherited by `location /` (nginx/nginx.conf:690-700), which serves the SPA route /teams (frontend/src/App.jsx:346-353). Only the Office snippet whitelists Microsoft ancestors (nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26). The committed Teams manifest points staticTabs/configurableTabs at https://getlawhand.com/teams and declares webApplicationInfo for SSO (teams-app/manifest.json:25-51). However, routers/teams.py has no SSO exchange (only link/notification/voice routes, lines 106-591). TeamsTabPage relies on cookie auth, and session cookies default to SameSite=Lax (backend/app/config.py:60). TASKS 1403 (SSO) is still pending (TASKS.md:2380-2389).
defects.user_impact: A firm admin who installs the checked-in lawhand-teams.zip gets a refused or blank LawHand tab in Teams, so the only Teams-embedded surface appears broken.

defects.title: Default Microsoft 365 storage lands in the connecting admin's personal OneDrive, contrary to the org-owned-root guarantee
defects.detail: In Auto mode, an active Microsoft 365 connection binds storage to OneDrive (TC-02, TASKS.md:567-569; RELEASE_NOTES.md:1735). The OneDrive root is `/me/drive` (backend/app/services/cloud_init.py:1506-1508), so it is the delegated admin's personal drive. The design of record promises that business-tenant roots are organisation-owned (docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:12-14) but rates OneDrive 'No — at risk' (line 28). SharePoint, the org-owned custody option, requires an explicit admin override, and its access is still delegated (lines 92-93). The at_risk warning mitigates this but does not prevent it.
defects.user_impact: For the Microsoft 365 first-customer profile, firm matter records live in one person's OneDrive. Custody and access are lost or disputed when that admin leaves or is deprovisioned.

defects.title: BK28/ECO ledger is stale: shipped work is still unchecked, and the plan's current-state gaps are outdated
defects.detail: The epic is headed '(PLANNED)' and every ECO item is [ ]. However, the ECO-17 substance (Personal Google mode) shipped (backend/app/routers/integrations.py:266-286; CHANGELOG.md:279-289). ECO-24 to ECO-28 largely shipped (docs/sms-provider-operations.md:11-40; propose_client_sms in workspace_mcp_protocol.py:124), and ECO-01/04 partially shipped (CHANGELOG.md:312-318, 752-758). The plan's leverage table still says 'personal Gmail directory sync fails' (plan:64). It also says signup's trial_ends_at is unread (plan:66, 262-265), which was fixed in 2026.09.11.8.
defects.user_impact: New M365/Google/Copilot recommendations measured against this ledger will duplicate or re-plan shipped work, and sequencing (e.g. ECO-17 as a P2 prerequisite for ECO-19) looks more expensive than it is.

defects.title: Docs understate granted mail scopes: code requests Mail.Send / gmail.send, docs say read-only
defects.detail: The setup doc lists the Microsoft admin/user scopes without Mail.Send and says Google consent covers 'Gmail read' (docs/integrations-setup.md:46-47, 71-72). The virtual document assistant plan states 'Existing Microsoft and Google mail integrations use read-only scopes' (docs/virtual-document-assistant-plan.md:544-545). The code requests Mail.Send and gmail.send in admin, user and solo scope sets (backend/app/routers/integrations.py:241-272; constants at backend/app/services/connected_mail.py:44-45) and sends via /me/sendMail and gmail messages/send.
defects.user_impact: The setup doc tells operators to record granted scopes in the customer security record, so customer security records and consent disclosures under-report send permission. ECO-18 Google scope verification planning starts from the wrong baseline.

defects.title: BYOK 'copilot'/'gemini' customer-LLM path contradicts ECO-20 and the LiteLLM-only ledger
defects.detail: A tenant admin endpoint 'Configure the tenant to use their own LLM subscription (Gemini/Copilot)' (backend/app/routers/admin.py:1515-1520) stores a key that bypasses the LiteLLM gateway entirely (backend/app/services/llm.py:261-275). Provider 'copilot' is actually an Azure OpenAI resource (backend/app/services/byok_security.py:33-58; config comment 'Azure OpenAI (Copilot backend)' at backend/app/config.py:155). The default Gemini model is hard-coded 'gemini-2.0-flash'. Gateway accounting metadata is skipped for customer keys (llm.py:351). This conflicts with TASKS.md:2622 ([x] direct Azure/Gemini paths removed) and with ECO-20 ('behind LiteLLM, never ... a subscription benefit or an unmetered tenant route', TASKS.md:479-481).
defects.user_impact: Naming and docstrings invite the ruled-out misconception that a firm's Microsoft 365 Copilot or Gemini subscription powers LawHand. The tenant route also escapes the gateway's approval, fallback and metering controls.

defects.title: Teams ledger stale and a build artifact committed against plan
defects.detail: 1402 (manifest/packaging) is marked PENDING although teams-app/manifest.json and package.ps1 exist. The same task says 'do not commit the zip', yet teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip is tracked (git ls-files). The launch list also requires updating Teams/Office manifests to new app IDs (TASKS.md:146), so a committed zip can silently drift from manifest.json.
defects.user_impact: Operators may sideload a stale zip with old app IDs, and planners see Teams packaging as not started.

defects.title: Office add-in roadmap has no live task entries; the only TASKS item refers to the removed prototype
defects.detail: TASKS says 'Ship the Word add-in properly (it hardcodes localhost ... localStorage) or archive it'. But word-addin/ was removed and replaced by office-addin/ (docs/office-document-assistant-plan.md:355; office-addin/README.md). The Office plan's Slices 1-5 (docs/office-document-assistant-plan.md:259-306) and the W2 Template Builder (docs/template-studio-clio-parity-execution-status.md:187-191) have no tracked TASKS entries.
defects.user_impact: The Word/Outlook/Excel roadmap, the main 'use the client's office suite' path, is invisible in the ledger and easy to drop or duplicate.

defects.title: Remediation plan status and migration references are wrong
defects.detail: The header still says 'Status: Proposed' although phases 0-2 are marked Done. It cites migrations '073_integration_observability' and '074' under migrations/versions (lines 31, 179, 195), but the real files are backend/alembic/versions/082_integration_observability.py and 083_matter_doc_storage_meta.py.

ux_findings.issue: Workspace MCP is the channel a firm would use to connect Claude/ChatGPT today and Copilot Studio/Gemini Enterprise later. It is labeled 'MCP servers', uses audience 'operator', and sits under Advanced (lines 34-43). Firm admins asking 'can we use our own AI assistant?' will not find it.
ux_findings.suggestion: Add a firm-audience card, 'Connected AI assistants', that shows the enablement state and a link to per-user connections. Keep policy controls operator-only. Name Copilot Studio as 'pilot' only after ECO-09.

ux_findings.issue: getTeamsLinks failures are caught and rendered as an empty 'Linked channels' list, so auth, framing and permission errors look like 'no channels' (also noted in docs/platform-feature-review-2026-09-06.md:46).
ux_findings.suggestion: Render a distinct error state with retry and a 'Sign in to LawHand' / 'Open in browser' fallback. Distinguish 403 (not admin/Teams not enabled) from empty.

ux_findings.issue: The option is labeled 'Personal Google / Google One'. Given the product owner's interest in 'leveraging Gemini', this implies a Google One (Gemini) subscription does something in LawHand, which the recorded decision rules out.
ux_findings.suggestion: Label it 'Personal Google account (Gmail)' and add one line: 'LawHand does not use Google One or Gemini subscriptions; AI runs on LawHand's approved routes.'

ux_findings.issue: The review's attachment gap is now fixed (EmailAttachments in ComposeEmailModal.jsx:141), but CC/BCC is still absent. Legal correspondence copied to the supervising attorney must be sent outside LawHand (via Outlook/Gmail), breaking the matter record.
ux_findings.suggestion: Add CC (and optionally BCC) to the connected-mailbox send path, or offer 'Create draft in Outlook/Gmail' (VA-6) so the user finishes in their own client.
